questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement real-world security gates that combine image scanning, attestation, and policy enforcement in a scalable multi‑tenant environment.

## Key Concepts

- Admission control with OPA/Kyverno
- SBOMs and CVE scoring via Trivy
- Image signing with cosign and Rekor attestation
- PR‑level gating and local verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: scan SBOM, sign, and publish attestation
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - name: Run Trivy SBOM
    run: trivy image --format cyclonedx -o sbom.json image:tag
  - name: Cosign sign SBOM
    run: cosign sign -key cosign.pub sbom.json
  - name: Rekor attestation
    run: cosign attest sbom.json --type sbom --format json
```

```yaml
# OPA policy (partial) enforcing CVE threshold and SBOM signing
package gate
default allow = false
allow {
  input.images[_].cve_score <= 6.0
  input.images[_].sbom_signed
}
```

```yaml
# Minimal manifest examples (one failing, one passing)

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-fail
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example/unsafe:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# passing: compliant image
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-pass
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example/secure:1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

- What thresholds would you adjust for prod vs. staging?
- How would you scale the gate across many clusters and tenants?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

### Follow-up
- Extend to handle missing tests per service gracefully
- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-web-egress
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  podSelector:

      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Egress

  - to:

  - to:

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CI policy enforcement skills using image signing—a common real-world requirement in production Kubernetes environments. It assesses understanding of supply chain security and GitOps practices.

## Key Concepts
- Container image signing with cosign
- Public key infrastructure for signature verification
- Manifest scanning in CI pipelines
- Handling signed vs. unsigned images in deployment gates
- GitOps workflow security

## Code Example

**GitHub Actions Workflow:**
```yaml
name: Verify Image Signatures
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'manifests/**'

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Extract image references
        id: images
        run: |
          echo "images=$(grep -roh 'registry.example.com/[^"]+' manifests/ | sort -u | jq -R -s -c '. | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          for image in $(echo '${{ steps.images.outputs.images }}' | jq -r '.[]'); do
            cosign verify --key cosign.pub $image
          done
```

**Sample Manifest (signed image):**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: myapp
        image: registry.example.com/myapp:v1.0.0
```

**Failing Manifest (unsigned):**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: myapp
        image: registry.example.com/myapp:unsigned
```

## Local Verification
```bash
# Generate key pair
cosign generate-key-pair

# Sign an image
cosign sign --key cosign.key registry.example.com/myapp:v1.0.0

# Verify locally
cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/myapp:v1.0.0
```

## CI Verification
The GitHub Actions workflow above automatically extracts all images from manifests and verifies each signature. The pipeline fails if any image lacks a valid signature, ensuring only trusted images are deployed.

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-world platforms enforce secure, auditable deployments at gate level. This tests policy design, cross-cloud concerns, and integration with canary delivery.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code: Kyverno/OPA
- Secrets management in Kubernetes
- Pod security basics and resource budgets
- Image provenance and canary verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Failing manifest (literal env)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-worker
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: myregistry/ml:tag
        env:
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "secret"
```
```yaml
# Passing manifest (secretRef / secret store)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-worker
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: myregistry/ml@sha256:...
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: ml-secret
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale the gate across 100s of services?
- How would you report gate violations to CI dashboards?
